chunks: ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah narrated from a shaykh from the family of Saʿd, who said:

There was between me and a man from the people of al-Madinah a dispute of great seriousness. So I entered upon Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and mentioned that to him, and I said: Teach me something by which Allah may perhaps restore to me my wrongfully taken right.

So he said: “When you seek to confront the enemy, then perform two rakʿahs or four rakʿahs between the grave and the minbar, or if you wish then in your house; and ask Allah to help you, and take something from whatever is easy for you, then give it in charity to the first needy person you meet.”
He said: So I did what he commanded me, and judgment was given in my favor, and Allah returned my land to me.

key_terms.الْقَبْرِ: the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in al-Madinah
key_terms.الْمِنْبَرِ: the pulpit in the Prophet’s mosque
key_terms.مَظْلِمَتِي: my wrongfully taken right or grievance

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach a person to seek Allah’s help in recovering a wrongfully taken right?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a dispute brought before Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام and his guidance to combine salat, du'a, and charity when seeking relief from oppression. It highlights turning to Allah through worship and almsgiving while seeking the restoration of one’s rights.
